column1: log K = log10(1e9 / M) + log10(n) - log10(Kd in uM), M = 66,463 g/mol for albumin

Read the Route column. Rows reach their log K by different routes, from a direct measurement to a conversion resting on an assumed stoichiometry. Two values in this column are not necessarily the same kind of number.

ligand:protein ratio is the molar loading the measurement was made at. Below ~0.01 the assay sees the specific site; above ~1 it increasingly sees non-specific partitioning. It is NOT always PFAS conc / protein conc. For Allendorf 2019 and Klevens 1954 the column is the paper's own reported BOUND ratio, moles of PFAS bound per mole of protein, not a dosing quotient -- Klevens plots exactly that quantity, 'Moles C8 Acid Bound per Mole BSA (MR)', and its 29 is where the binding curve breaks, not a concentration anyone dosed. That is why those rows leave PFAS conc blank: multiplying the ratio by the protein concentration would manufacture a dose out of a bound stoichiometry. For ITC studies the two concentrations are in different vessels.
